bankinu
•
5d ago

How do you solve this problem -

"Let me read (some file already read)"

And then it proceeds to print contents of a large part of the file it read using decode tokens. I haven't seen previous Qwen or any other model do this.

Reducing to medium or low didn't solve this.

Fedor_Doc
•
5d ago
•
Edited 5d ago

Deepseek v4 Flash does it. It increases weight of the cited part in the reasoning -> less hallucinations about the code. Useful with optimized attention architectures.

kaelwd
•
5d ago

I wish it would just actually re-read the file though, prefill is 20x faster than decode and there's 0% chance of hallucinations.

simcop2387
•
5d ago

I haven't really benchmarked yet but this might be a great spot for llama.cpp's ngram-map-k or ngram-map-k4v speculative decoders. What I'm not familiar with enough though is how to tune them or how they'll work with the native MTP. I know you can specify multiple of them together though.

kaelwd
•
3d ago

I tried ngram-mod a while ago but acceptance rate was always abysmal so it had a negative affect overall from the verification overhead. When it works you do get like triple the throughput which is nice but still slower than just reading the file again.

1 more reply
michaelsoft__binbows
•
5d ago

kinda funny this mirrors our own operation as well. like the context window is just your short term buffer of your brain, not some notebook on your desk or whatever. Re-read something, yeah it's getting blitted out into the context window too.

the fact that we can fully control the context window is so powerful and we're like only scratching the surface of what we can do.

bankinu
•
5d ago

But it doesn't actually reread.

"Let me read..." And then it prints something out already read long back, verbatim.

Your point may still hold though, it's almost like "let me recall". But where it differs from us is that it recollects verbatim - which means it was there in the context window very clearly without attenuation.

AnOnlineHandle
•
5d ago

Seems like there's a place for architectures which allow setting higher attention scores on given tokens in the prior text for some segment of next predicted tokens, rather than having to reprint it all.

Lakius_2401
•
5d ago

It's trying to mimic a stream of consciousness, and "reading" in a stream of consciousness is literally interrupting the flow with verbatim context. If a stream of consciousness says "let me read" and doesn't show the text, it didn't read it, it lied and is operating off memory.

Whether CoT with verbatim token duplication is an ideal technique or not remains to be settled (though the benchmarks seem to agree, and many CoT's that don't do that felt useless to me). In terms of token acceleration, draft techniques make that significantly less resource intense. Alibaba's Qwen team has shifted the balance from a huge and powerful KV cache solution over to a more processing intense solution. Qwen 3.8 sips memory for cache but "wastes" tokens to optimize attention live.

Researchers are refining techniques to dynamically and meaningfully optimize context attention, and Qwen 3.8's stopgap answer is "the model will do it live".

As an aside, you could replace every instance of "let me read/reference/look" in the training data to call it something more LLM specific, but I think you'd see a regression in output quality as it would have less broad examples of what it's accomplishing or trying to mimic when it says that. <think> blocks aren't for you.
